title: Ticketly Backlog
description: A generated backlog: an optional company, a project, its estimation model, and its epics and tickets. Single source of truth for every Ticketly renderer and validator. A backlog with no `estimation` block is a legacy Fibonacci backlog and validates exactly as before; `estimation.model` selects the ticket shape: `fibonacci` (Fibonacci story points) or `hours` (hours-based points calculated from a standard-hour estimate and a difficulty level).

company.description: Company / organization this backlog is for. OPTIONAL. When present it must be the real name the user provides — Ticketly never invents it. Omit it entirely on an existing-project run (where asking for a company is awkward); the backlog is then titled by its project name alone.

project.description: Project name this backlog belongs to, supplied by the user, e.g. 'Demo Project'.

tickets.description: Epics and Tasks. Their shape depends on the estimation model (see allOf).

id.description: Epics: EPIC-<PREFIX> (e.g. EPIC-ARC). Tasks: <PREFIX>-NNN (e.g. ARC-001). Prefix is the epic theme; children inherit it.

status.description: To Do, In Progress, In Review (waiting for review), Done. Done means the work was reviewed and meets its acceptance criteria.

estimation.description: Which estimation model this backlog uses, chosen once when the backlog is created. Changing it is an explicit, recorded action (`ticketly switch-model`).

model.description: hours = hours-based points; fibonacci = Fibonacci story points.

rubric_version.description: Hours model: the difficulty rubric new estimates are made under (e.g. 'hours-v1').

rubrics.description: Hours model: every difficulty rubric used by an estimate in this backlog, frozen by version, so a later calibration never rescores existing estimates.

history.description: Every model change: when, from, to, and why.

rubric.description: Difficulty multipliers by level, as exact decimal strings (e.g. '1.10').

estimate.description: Hours model: the inputs effort is calculated from. Points = estimated_hours x the difficulty multiplier, rounded half-up to one decimal. Estimates describe the work, never the person doing it.

estimated_hours.description: Standard hours: active work for a developer competent in the stack and familiar with the project to meet the acceptance criteria — implementation, testing, self-review and handoff. Excludes waiting and person-specific onboarding. Must equal the breakdown total; in a CSV it is computed from the breakdown columns. Numbers must be finite.

difficulty_level.description: 1 Basic (x1.00), 2 Standard (x1.10), 3 Complex (x1.25), 4 Advanced (x1.40), chosen from technical evidence — never because a task is long. A whole number; 2.0 reads as 2.

difficulty_reason.description: Short, task-specific evidence for the chosen level.

estimate_confidence.description: high = scope and approach established; medium = bounded assumptions remain; low = material questions unresolved. Does not change points.

rubric_version.description: The rubric this estimate was made under; its multipliers are frozen in estimation.rubrics.

work_kind.description: Optional. Marks substantial cleanup, integration, client preparation, or a bounded investigation as its own explicit task. Leave it out for ordinary build work; routine testing and self-review stay inside the original task's estimate.

split_from.description: Optional. This Task was split out of another Task (partial completion handed to someone else). scope 'replaced' = it takes over scope the original was estimated for: the original's estimate must be reduced to the work it keeps (it must keep some — a full takeover is a reassignment, not a split), and the whole chain of replaced splits may never total more than the root was estimated at before the first split, plus growth recorded with approved_by. scope 'additional' = genuinely new, approved scope.

approved_by.description: Who approved additional scope. Expected when the new task has the same owner as the original.

legacy_estimate.description: The estimate a Task had before its backlog switched models, with its owner and status at the time. Legacy points are reported separately and never added to the new model's totals. A Task that was completed at the switch keeps its legacy points, credited to the owner recorded here, and can't be re-estimated; new work on it belongs in a new Task.

history_event.description: One recorded change. 'baseline' records the starting estimate, owner and status; later events record estimate, assignee, status and model changes. Earlier snapshots are never erased.

split_to.description: Tasks that took over part of this Task's scope when this estimate was reduced.

approved_by.description: Who approved this estimate increase (`ticketly recalc --approved-by`). Only approved growth lets a split family total more than its root was estimated at before the split.

history.description: Recorded by `ticketly recalc`, `ticketly import` and `ticketly switch-model`.

ticket.description: A ticket in a legacy backlog (no estimation block): Fibonacci effort, exactly as before.

title.description: Short task name, e.g. 'Backup restore and rollback drill'.

type.description: Epic groups child tickets; Task is a unit of work.

parent.description: For Tasks: the EPIC-<PREFIX> id this belongs to. For Epics: null.

effort.description: Fibonacci story points. Epics use 0 (sized via their children).

dependencies.description: Ids of tickets that must be done first. Empty array if none.

description.description: Clear statement of intent / what and why.

acceptance_criteria.description: Testable, closeable conditions. Required (non-empty) for Tasks; may be empty for Epics.

needs_clarification.description: Guardrail: true when requirements were too thin and scope was NOT invented. Flag instead of hallucinating.

assignee.description: Optional. Person responsible, or null/unassigned. Hidden by default for small/solo teams.

due_date.description: Optional ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or null. Hidden by default.

fibonacci_ticket.description: A ticket in a backlog whose estimation model is 'fibonacci': the legacy ticket plus ownership/progress tracking fields.

hours_ticket.description: A ticket in a backlog whose estimation model is 'hours'. effort is the calculated points (one decimal), null when the Task is Unestimated; Epics keep effort 0 and are totalled from their children.

effort.description: Calculated points (hours x difficulty multiplier, rounded half-up to one decimal). Never typed by hand: `ticketly recalc` and `ticketly import` set it. null = Unestimated. Epics: 0.

estimate.description: The estimate inputs; null when the Task is Unestimated.
